sm: The host opens by noting that Thanksgiving is approaching, a time to give thanks for the United States, and says some people on TikTok are thankful in a different way. He plays a video in which a creator says Native Americans are America's guilty conscience and that they have survived 500 years of efforts to erase their history. The host answers that he doesn't think about it that way. He says it was not a genocide but a series of wars and the spread of disease, and he asks what anti-Native hatred in America today even looks like. He questions what is meant by stolen land, pointing out that conquest and migration happened on the continent long before Europeans arrived. He also jokes about people condemning the West while filming on iPhones, and about a clip of a woman in a low-cut top with a Land Back shirt.

The host then reacts to claims that World War II might never have happened without the treatment of Native Americans, and that Hitler drew inspiration from westward expansion. He says Nazi sources more often cited the Armenian genocide, and that American eugenics policies of the early twentieth century were a likelier inspiration for Nazi racial policy. He also mentions a Columbia professor who made a similar claim about Lincoln. He argues that history includes large conquests and slavery elsewhere, such as the Muslim conquests, which people ignore depending on the intersectional hierarchy. Next he plays a clip complaining that America is named for the Italian Amerigo Vespucci, and he replies that Europeans bringing technology to the hemisphere was a major moment in history. In a final clip he hears the slogan that nobody is illegal on stolen land. He replies that if land belongs to no one, it does not belong to the speaker either. He closes by saying America has flaws, but on Thanksgiving people should thank a country that is a great force for good.
